title: Emitted Core gzip growth past the 10% review trigger for the Http cache mode, protocol 1.5 (RQ-LIMEN-2026-A008, WI-0175)
proposedAddition: No new concept, file, primitive, family, root export or dependency. The existing Core Http effect gains one optional request field, HttpEffectRequest.cache, of one new contract enum, HttpCacheMode (default, no-store, no-cache, reload), and the kernel adds one spread line passing it to fetch's cache init. The generated core codec gains its decoder and the closed field list one name. Measured by npm run check:core-budget on 2026-10-24: emitted Core gzip bytes 25885 on origin/main 1cf75cb (+10.0% over the approved 23540, nine bytes under the trigger) -> 25999 on claude/http-cache-mode (+10.4%). The proposal is that the owner approve this growth, so that a later guardrail work item may re-approve the baseline in architecture/core-baseline.json citing this record.
invariantOrUseCase: typed-capabilities and explicit effects: every request the engine asks for behaves exactly as the engine reasons about it. Without a cache mode, the browser HTTP cache can answer a read of a mutable resource with a stored response the server marked cacheable, so the engine sees an answer the server would no longer give. Observed twice (indy-init rehearsals 2 and 3, defect class DC-005): GitHub's commits/main answers cache-control: private, max-age=60, and a cached 200 hid the 401 that followed a token change. The engine had no typed way to refuse the cache; the consumer busted every mutable URL with a ?fresh=<nonce> query.
whyNotHtmlCss: The request is made by the kernel's fetch call; no markup or style reaches it.
whyNotEngineLibrary: An engine library can only shape the request the engine sends; how fetch meets the HTTP cache is decided inside the kernel's one fetch call. The library-only workaround, a cache-busting query, changes the URL the server sees and pollutes the cache with one entry per nonce.
whyNotCapabilityPack: A pack would be a second, competing Http path for one fetch init property, which docs/43-http-profiles.md already rules out for credentials and the other 1.3 options: they are properties of the one fetch call the Core Http effect makes.
whyNotForma: Forma owns interaction and presentation primitives, not network requests. (Forma was not consulted from this session.)
whyNotGovernedAdapter: An adapter wraps a third-party rendering surface; it has no part in Core Http requests.
whyNotTooling: The stale response happens at runtime in the browser; no build or check can prevent it.
whyNotHostRenderer: Every host runs the same kernel Http effect; a host-specific cache policy would make the same engine request behave differently by host, and would put a decision in the host.

consumerEvidence.consumer: indy-init (rehearsals 2 and 3), an F# Limen application reading GitHub
consumerEvidence.evidence: Its research/rehearsal-003-defect-analysis.md D-07/M2 and src/services/GitHub.fs: a cached commits/main 200 masked a 401 after a token change; worked around with a per-request ?fresh=<nonce> query

complexityDelta: Measured 2026-10-24, npm run check:core-budget, origin/main 1cf75cb -> claude/http-cache-mode: handwritten Core lines 967 -> 969; generated Core lines 861 -> 865 (+2.1% -> +2.6% over the approved 843: the enum, its decoder and encoder); emitted Core gzip bytes 25885 -> 25999 (+114; +10.0% -> +10.4% over approved, the only dimension past a threshold); root exports 59, root export families 6, protocol union variants 42, binding primitives 6, built-in capability families 4, runtime dependencies 0, canonical concepts 7, minimal graph modules 10, all unchanged. Payload consequence: bench/budgets.json kernel-with-store goes from 35830 to 35872 gzip bytes bundled, 32 over its 35840 budget (its baseline, 32118, predates the in-budget kernel growth since WI-0136), so the guardrail work item that re-approves the Core baseline should also re-baseline the kernel-loading payload profiles, as WI-0136 did.
compatibilityImpact: Wire-additive and absent by default: a request without cache is the 1.4 request, byte for byte. The contract fingerprint changes and PROTOCOL_MINOR becomes 5, so engines regenerate their bindings; F# record and C# positional constructions of HttpEffectRequest, and Rust struct literals, must name the new field (Cache = None / null / cache: None). An engine must send cache only to a kernel that negotiated 1.5: an older WebAssembly transport's closed decoder refuses the field.
negativeBoundaryTests: Unchanged and passing on the branch: test/core-boundary.test.ts (no Core file outside architecture/core.json, Core imports no optional layer); npm run check:architecture, check:layers and check:typescript pass. test/core-budget.test.ts fails only on the review trigger this record asks about: each negative case reports its own violation plus 'review-trigger: emitted Core gzip bytes'.
guestLanguageImpact: All four bindings are regenerated by npm run contract:generate. F# gains HttpCacheMode (Default | NoStore | NoCache | Reload) and HttpEffectRequest.Cache: HttpCacheMode option; C# a nullable HttpCacheMode? Cache parameter; Rust an Option<HttpCacheMode> field. The shared vectors (64) pass in F# and C#, the Rust binding tests pass, the minimal engines' sessions match, and guest compile pressure holds.
